broadcasts.message: normalize.js implemented per spec: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. No extra changes. Ready for integration.

tokenizer.js implemented: tokenize(text) calls injected normalize(text) once, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes using regex /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g, preserving order and negation. Returns empty array for no matches. Ready for integration.

pipeline.js ready. processText calls injected tokenize, builds exact result object. Frequencies uses Object.create(null) to safely handle 'constructor' and other prototype keys. Unique preserves first-seen order. No shadowing of dependencies. Ready for integration.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 1: I own normalize.js. Requirements: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. No other changes. Must not shadow injected normalize (I don't declare it). Must return JSON with files, memory, message. Need to ensure robust handling for null/non-string? Spec says 'for string input' but host likely passes string; still guard. Use String.prototype.normalize('NFKC') to handle unicode. Collapse whitespace: replace /\s+/g with ' ' after trimming? Actually collapse then trim. Use regex /\s+/g. Lowercase after NFKC? Order: NFKC, lowercase, collapse, trim. Fine. No dependencies. Next rounds: expect peers' tokenize/processText.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 1: Implement tokenizer.js per spec. Key decisions: tokenize calls injected normalize(text) once, then uses regex /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g to extract tokens in order. No stopwords, preserve negation. Ensure no shadowing of normalize. Will coordinate with normalize/pipeline peers. Future rounds: verify interface compatibility, handle edge cases.
private_memories.integrator: Round 1: Integrator role. Own pipeline.js. Must implement processText(text) that calls injected tokenize(text). Requirements: return {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}; text = tokens.join(' '); tokens = token array from tokenize; count = tokens.length; unique = first-seen distinct tokens; frequencies = object mapping each token to count, must handle prototype names (e.g., 'constructor' key). No shadowing of normalize/tokenize. No extra functions. Keep faithful. Peers: normalize.js and tokenizer.js expected to follow spec. Next rounds: verify compatibility, no changes unless needed.
